::: {.callout-warning appearance="simple"}
Educational simulation only. These are **scripted teaching scenarios**, not real patients, and
the branching logic and outcomes are a teaching model — treat any disagreement with your
attending or your institution's protocol as the authority. **Do not enter patient
information.**
:::

A growing library of short branching scenarios. Each one is built around a **single core EVD
concept** — mostly the periprocedural window, when an aneurysmal SAH patient with an EVD leaves
the unit for the interventional suite. You make a series of decisions; each choice changes what
happens next, and some paths recover while others cascade.

Airway, anesthetic technique, and detailed hemodynamic management are relevant and assumed —
they are deliberately **out of scope** here. Every decision is about the drain.

## Scenarios in this set

| Scenario | Core concept |
|---|---|
| **The blind transport** | Never move a clamped EVD without a way to see the ICP. |
| **Rising ICP on transport — the troubleshoot** | Is it real → is it mechanical → is it the patient — *then* drain, osmotherapy, escalate. |
| **Open EVD: 18 mL in 15 minutes** | A drainage rate well above baseline is acute over-drainage until proven otherwise — clamp first. |
| **Re-zeroing after every move** | Zeroing is valid only for the position it was done in; re-level to the tragus after every transfer. |
| **The CSF turns bloody** | Intra-procedurally the drain is an early-warning monitor — a colour or output change is a real-time call-out. |
| **The handoff gap** | The minimum EVD dataset a receiving team needs, and what breaks when one item is missing. |
